organicRemedies.name: Copper-based organic fungicide spray
organicRemedies.instructions: Spray a copper hydroxide or copper oxychloride organic-approved formulation over foliage, ensuring full leaf coverage including undersides.

organicRemedies.name: Crop rotation and sanitation
organicRemedies.instructions: Rotate away from potato/tomato family crops for at least 2 seasons; remove and destroy (do not compost) all infected plant debris immediately after harvest.

chemicalRemedies.name: Mancozeb-based fungicide
chemicalRemedies.instructions: Apply as a protective foliar spray before infection establishes; do not apply after visible sporulation has spread widely.
chemicalRemedies.dosage: 2-2.5 g per litre of water (follow product label for your region)
chemicalRemedies.safetyPrecautions: Wear gloves and a mask; avoid spraying in windy conditions; keep children and livestock away from treated fields until spray has dried.

chemicalRemedies.name: Chlorothalonil fungicide
chemicalRemedies.instructions: Use as an alternate rotation partner with Mancozeb to reduce resistance build-up.
chemicalRemedies.dosage: 2 g per litre of water (follow product label for your region)
chemicalRemedies.safetyPrecautions: Avoid inhalation and skin contact; wash hands thoroughly after application; do not apply within the pre-harvest interval.

organicRemedies.name: Neem oil spray
organicRemedies.instructions: Mix cold-pressed neem oil with a mild soap emulsifier and water; spray on affected foliage in the early morning or evening.

organicRemedies.name: Mulching and lower-leaf pruning
organicRemedies.instructions: Remove lower leaves touching soil and apply straw mulch to reduce soil splash that spreads spores onto foliage.

chemicalRemedies.name: Azoxystrobin fungicide
chemicalRemedies.instructions: Apply at first sign of concentric leaf-spot lesions; rotate with a different mode-of-action fungicide to prevent resistance.
chemicalRemedies.dosage: 1 ml per litre of water (follow product label for your region)
chemicalRemedies.safetyPrecautions: Toxic to aquatic life; do not apply near water bodies; use recommended PPE.

organicRemedies.name: Balanced nitrogen management
organicRemedies.instructions: Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser, which increases susceptibility; split nitrogen doses across growth stages instead of one heavy application.

organicRemedies.name: Field drainage management
organicRemedies.instructions: Avoid prolonged standing water and ensure fields drain well after heavy rain, since the pathogen spreads readily in waterlogged conditions.

chemicalRemedies.name: Copper oxychloride + Streptocycline
chemicalRemedies.instructions: Apply as a combined spray at early symptom onset; this bactericide combination is the standard extension recommendation for bacterial leaf blight in rice.
chemicalRemedies.dosage: Copper oxychloride 3 g/L + Streptocycline 1 g in 15 L water (follow product label / local KVK advisory)
chemicalRemedies.safetyPrecautions: Do not mix with alkaline pesticides; wear gloves and eye protection; avoid spraying during flowering to protect pollinators.

organicRemedies.name: Silicon soil amendment
organicRemedies.instructions: Apply calcium silicate slag or rice-husk ash to paddy soil; silicon uptake strengthens leaf tissue against fungal penetration.
organicRemedies.applicationFrequency: Once per season, at land preparation

chemicalRemedies.name: Tricyclazole fungicide
chemicalRemedies.instructions: Apply preventively at boot-leaf stage and again at early heading, the two most vulnerable growth stages for panicle blast.
chemicalRemedies.dosage: 0.6 g per litre of water (follow product label for your region)
chemicalRemedies.safetyPrecautions: Follow the pre-harvest interval strictly for a food crop; store away from food and animal feed.

organicRemedies.name: Resistant variety rotation
organicRemedies.instructions: Where the disease recurs, rotate to a rust-resistant wheat variety recommended by your local agricultural university for the next sowing.

chemicalRemedies.name: Propiconazole fungicide
chemicalRemedies.instructions: Apply at first appearance of yellow striping on leaves; a second spray 15 days later if humid weather persists.
chemicalRemedies.dosage: 1 ml per litre of water (follow product label for your region)
chemicalRemedies.safetyPrecautions: Wheat rust spreads via windborne spores across large areas rapidly; report outbreaks to your local agriculture office in addition to treating your own field.

organicRemedies.name: Residue management / tillage
organicRemedies.instructions: Plough under or remove crop residue after harvest, since the fungus overwinters on infected maize debris.

chemicalRemedies.name: Pyraclostrobin + Metconazole fungicide
chemicalRemedies.instructions: Apply between tasseling and silking if lesions are spreading up the canopy.
chemicalRemedies.dosage: 1 ml per litre of water (follow product label for your region)
chemicalRemedies.safetyPrecautions: Use protective eyewear; avoid application within 24 hours of expected rainfall for effectiveness.

organicRemedies.name: Remove and destroy infected trees
organicRemedies.instructions: There is currently no cure for Huanglongbing. Infected trees should be removed and destroyed promptly to reduce the source of infection for the Asian citrus psyllid vector.

organicRemedies.name: Psyllid vector control via reflective mulch
organicRemedies.instructions: Use reflective foil mulch around young, uninfected trees to reduce psyllid landing rates while the orchard is monitored.

chemicalRemedies.name: Vector (psyllid) control insecticide
chemicalRemedies.activeIngredient: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (soil drench, uninfected trees only)
chemicalRemedies.instructions: This treats the insect vector, not the disease itself, and should only be used on healthy trees near a confirmed outbreak, under guidance from your local plant protection office.
chemicalRemedies.dosage: As per local extension advisory; do not self-apply without consulting authorities given quarantine implications
chemicalRemedies.preHarvestIntervalDays: N/A - vector control on non-fruiting or pre-harvest trees
chemicalRemedies.safetyPrecautions: This is a quarantine-notifiable disease in most regions. Contact your regional plant quarantine / agriculture authority before taking action, in addition to any treatment.

organicRemedies.name: Quarantine and destroy infected mats
organicRemedies.instructions: There is no cure once a plant is infected. Isolate the affected area, avoid moving soil, tools, or planting material off-site, and destroy infected plants in place.

organicRemedies.name: Biosecurity / footwear disinfection
organicRemedies.instructions: Disinfect boots and tools with a quaternary ammonium or chlorine-based footbath before and after entering the affected plot to avoid spreading spores.

organicRemedies.name: Potassium bicarbonate spray
organicRemedies.instructions: Dissolve potassium bicarbonate in water with a horticultural-oil surfactant and spray over affected canopy; disrupts fungal cell walls on contact.

organicRemedies.name: Canopy management
organicRemedies.instructions: Prune to open the canopy and improve airflow, reducing the humid microclimate the fungus needs to spread.

chemicalRemedies.name: Sulfur-based fungicide
chemicalRemedies.instructions: Apply in cooler parts of the day; do not apply within 2 weeks of an oil spray or in temperatures above 32°C to avoid leaf scorch.
chemicalRemedies.dosage: 2-3 g per litre of water (follow product label for your region)
chemicalRemedies.safetyPrecautions: Avoid combining with oil-based sprays; irritant to eyes and skin.

organicRemedies.name: Fallen leaf removal
organicRemedies.instructions: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn, since the fungus overwinters in leaf litter and releases spores in spring.

chemicalRemedies.name: Captan fungicide
chemicalRemedies.instructions: Apply protectively from green-tip stage through petal fall, the primary infection period for apple scab.
chemicalRemedies.dosage: 2 g per litre of water (follow product label for your region)
chemicalRemedies.safetyPrecautions: Wear gloves; avoid contact with eyes; do not apply during bloom to protect pollinating bees.

organicRemedies.name: Seed treatment sanitation
organicRemedies.instructions: Use only certified, disease-free seed and treat seed with hot water (52°C for 10 minutes) before sowing to kill seed-borne bacteria.

chemicalRemedies.name: Copper oxychloride spray
chemicalRemedies.instructions: Spray at first appearance of angular water-soaked leaf spots; repeat if wet weather continues.
chemicalRemedies.dosage: 3 g per litre of water (follow product label for your region)
chemicalRemedies.safetyPrecautions: Wear gloves and eye protection; avoid spraying in direct midday sun.

organicRemedies.name: Routine preventive monitoring
organicRemedies.instructions: No treatment needed. Continue periodic visual inspection, balanced fertilisation, and proper irrigation to maintain plant health.
